audience.a: The platform serves universities and schools and institutes and training centres as well as organisations that train their staff. The terminology of every screen follows the institution type. A university sees faculties and departments while a school sees stages and grades.

joining.a: Joining begins with a request through the contact page. We then discuss the institution type and student numbers and academic requirements. An independent environment is established with its own terminology and default language and its administrator is invited to it.

accounts.a: There is no open registration. An account is created only by the institution through an invitation link or directly by an authorised staff member. Members sign in with their email address or with the member ID their institution issues. An account created directly receives a temporary password that must be changed at the first sign in.

requirements.a: The platform runs in the browser on computers and phones and requires no installation. A proctored examination also needs access to the camera and the microphone with the student’s consent.

aiDrafts.a: The instructor uploads their own material as a PDF or Word or PowerPoint file or as images of pages including scanned ones. The platform builds a structured lesson draft from it. A lesson can also be drafted from a title and examination questions can be proposed with model answers. Artificial intelligence is called only when the instructor asks.

review.a: Everything artificial intelligence produces remains a draft until the instructor reviews it and edits it and approves it. Nothing reaches students without the instructor’s decision and the instructor remains responsible for the published content.

structure.a: Each course is divided into units and each unit holds its lessons. A lesson may combine text and images and video and mind maps and flashcards and short quizzes. The institution arranges its academic structure in two levels and assigns its students to groups.

languages.a: Interfaces and email messages and reports are available in Arabic and English with a right to left layout for Arabic. Each user chooses a preferred language and the institution sets its default language.

timing.a: The start time is recorded on the server when the student begins. Refreshing the page or changing the device clock does not change the remaining time. Questions and their options can be shown in a different order to each student.

grading.a: Model answers stay on the server and never reach the student’s browser. Multiple choice and true or false questions are graded on the server from the stored answers. Essay answers are graded by the instructor and students see their grades once they are published.

proctoring.a: Proctoring is enabled for each examination separately and the student consents before it starts. Detection runs on the student’s own device and covers the face and gaze and phones and books and additional people and speech and leaving the examination window. No camera image is sent for analysis and no artificial intelligence provider sees the camera.

evidence.q: What is recorded and for how long
evidence.a: Monitoring events are kept as short text entries. Evidence is limited to a ten second room check at the start and to a still image or a short clip for a serious violation or at the request of the exam teacher. Only the exam teacher can view it. It is stored outside the platform database and deleted permanently after 30 hours. Live viewing by the teacher is never recorded.

appeals.a: A flag alerts the instructor and is not a final ruling. The student can appeal any recorded violation in writing. The exam teacher reviews the event and decides the appeal with a written reply that the student can read.

isolation.a: Each institution’s data is isolated from all others in the database itself and not in the interface alone. Every read and write is restricted to the user’s own institution. Data is used only to run the platform and protect examination integrity and is never sold or shared for marketing.

access.a: Administrators see statistical indicators without the content of questions or student answers or individual grades. Instructors see their own groups and examinations. Students see their own content and their grades once published. No user can grant themselves a permission.

aiPrivacy.a: Names and contact details and identifiers and links are removed from a student’s text before it reaches an artificial intelligence provider. Camera images never reach any such provider. Providers are called only when a user asks.

cookies.a: The platform sets only the cookies needed to keep you signed in and to remember the language and appearance you chose. It sets no advertising cookies and no third party tracking cookies. The full list is in the cookie policy.

roles.a: Each institution has an administrator and a centre manager and instructors and students. The administrator grants the centre manager only the permissions the role requires such as managing students or courses or attendance or announcements or timetables or reports. No one can grant a permission they do not hold and permissions are verified on the server before every sensitive operation.

communication.a: Authorised staff prepare a weekly timetable for each group and publish it to its students. Announcements appear as cards to the students of a chosen audience and their wording can be suggested by artificial intelligence on request.

reports.a: Each course has an analysis of strengths and weaknesses with recommendations derived from fixed published rules. Staff follow attendance and progress and participation and each instructor can export the grades of their groups as a spreadsheet. Administrators see indicators for the whole institution.

archive.a: Deleting an item moves it to the institution’s archive instead of erasing it. The archive keeps the academic record across the years and items can be recovered from it when needed.

afterContact.a: We reply to the email address you provide. If you wish we arrange an introductory presentation drawn from your institution. We then configure the environment together with the institution and accompany its staff until work on the platform is well established.

pricing.a: Plans and prices are not published yet. They are agreed directly with each institution according to its size and needs.

demo.a: The demonstration shows the screens of each role with illustrative data and needs no account. You can also request an introductory presentation through the contact page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy

body: Account data such as your name and email address. We also keep your role and the institution you belong to.
Educational content created on the platform. This means lessons and exams together with answers and grades.
Monitoring data from monitored exams only. These are events such as switching windows or more than one face in front of the camera.
The camera image is analyzed on the student’s own device. We do not record or keep video.

After a serious violation a small still image is taken that only the exam teacher can see. There are no more than ten such images per student in each exam. They are kept by an independent cloud storage provider outside the platform database and permanently deleted 30 hours after capture.
During live monitoring the video reaches the teacher only while the exam is running. This stream is not recorded.
We use it to run the platform. That means showing lessons and grading exams. It also means publishing grades and sending invitations.
We use monitoring events to protect the integrity of exams. They are reviewed by the course teacher.
We never sell your data or share it with anyone for marketing.
The data of each institution is separated from the others at the database level. No user can see the data of another institution.
Students see only the content of their own group. Teachers see only their own groups.
Data is hosted with Supabase on AWS servers in Frankfurt and with Vercel. It is encrypted in transit and at rest.
Administrative access is limited to the platform owner. Sensitive operations run on the server and never in the browser.
You can ask for your data to be corrected or your account to be deleted. Contact your institution admin or write to us directly.
When an institution is removed from the platform the data of its users is deleted.
For any privacy question use the Contact page.

sections.summary: Grades cannot be forged from the browser.

sections.summary: Small text files the browser keeps for a site.

sections.summary: Five cookies and all of them are necessary or functional.

hero.title: An academic platform founded on integrity and clarity
hero.desc: Tilmoo was created to give educational institutions a single digital environment that protects assessment integrity and student privacy. It also makes content preparation and the follow up of learning easier for instructors.

pillars.label: Mission
pillars.text: To enable educational institutions to manage and assess teaching and learning in a trusted digital environment that protects the rights of everyone involved.

pillars.label: Vision
pillars.text: For Tilmoo to become a digital environment that institutions rely on to deliver education that is fair and accessible in Arabic and English.

pillars.label: Values
pillars.text: Integrity and privacy and clarity and accessibility and responsibility in everything we design and build.

principles.title: The principles on which the platform is built
principles.desc: Each of the following principles has a tangible effect on how the platform works. Select a principle to see how it is applied.
principles.applyLabel: How it is applied in the platform

items.title: Academic integrity
items.statement: Assessment integrity is not left to good faith alone. It is protected by technical safeguards that cannot be bypassed from the browser.
applications: Examination time is measured and grading is performed on the server.
Model answers never reach the student's device at any stage.
Results are recorded only through server services after verification.

items.title: Privacy by design
items.statement: Every feature is designed to collect as little data as possible and to keep what it collects where it belongs.
applications: The camera is analysed on the student's device and the stream is never sent to a server for analysis.
Administrators see statistical indicators without question or answer content.
Linking institutional mail requests permission to send only and never to read messages.

items.title: People make the decisions
items.statement: Technology assists instructors but never takes the decisions that affect students on their behalf.
applications: Instructors review all generated content before it is released.
Essay answers are graded by the instructor.
Instructors decide every appeal against a flag.

items.title: Isolation between institutions
items.statement: Each institution's data belongs to that institution alone and never intersects with the data of others.
applications: Isolation is enforced in the database at the level of every record.
Access attempts between institutions are tested to confirm that they fail.
Accounts are created only through an invitation from the institution itself.

items.title: Linguistic accessibility
items.statement: Arabic is a native language of the platform and not a later translation. English is available to the same extent.
applications: Complete interfaces and messages and reports in both languages.
Text direction changes automatically with the language.
A default language per institution and freedom of choice for every user.

items.title: Preserving the academic record
items.statement: The academic record is the institution's memory and should remain preserved across the years.
applications: Deleted items move to an archive from which they can be recovered.
A student's progress in an earlier course is preserved when they move between groups.
Records of earlier years can be consulted at any time.

community.title: Designed for everyone who contributes to learning

items.text: A complete view of institutional indicators and tools to manage accounts and permissions.
Tools for courses and enrolment and attendance within defined permissions.
Less time spent on preparation and more time for teaching and individual follow up.
A clear environment for lessons and examinations and results with safeguards that protect their rights.

hero.title: Security and privacy at the heart of the platform
hero.desc: This page explains the technical safeguards that protect assessment integrity and the confidentiality of institutional and student data. These safeguards are enforced on the server and in the database and not in the interface alone.

explorer.title: Select a risk to see the safeguard that addresses it

threats.title: Forging grades
threats.safeguard: Grades are computed on the server from the model answers stored there. User accounts have no direct write access to result tables.

threats.title: Extending examination time
threats.safeguard: The start time of an examination is recorded on the server when it begins. Refreshing the page or changing the device clock does not change the remaining time.

threats.title: Viewing another institution's data
threats.safeguard: Every read and write in the database is restricted to the user's own institution. Access attempts between institutions have been tested to confirm that they fail.

threats.title: Granting oneself permissions
threats.safeguard: Role and permission columns are pinned in the database so users cannot change their own. Permissions are verified on the server before every sensitive operation.

threats.title: Joining without authorisation
threats.safeguard: Accounts are created only with a valid invitation from the institution. Google is used for signing in only and never for creating accounts.

threats.title: Leaking student images
threats.safeguard: The camera stream is analysed inside the student's browser. Only small snapshots are sent for serious violations and only the exam teacher sees them through temporary links before they are permanently deleted after 30 hours.

threats.title: Accidental deletion
threats.safeguard: Data is never permanently erased. It moves to an institutional archive from which it can be recovered.

threats.title: Overuse of services
threats.safeguard: Rate limits apply to costly operations for each user separately.

items.title: User browser
items.desc: The camera is analysed locally and model answers never reach the browser at any stage.

items.title: Access gate
items.desc: Every page verifies the user's identity and account status and role before it is shown.

items.title: Server services
items.desc: Sensitive operations run only after checking permissions and confirming that the data belongs to the user's institution.

items.title: Database

hero.title: Artificial intelligence that assists instructors and never replaces them
hero.desc: The platform uses artificial intelligence to prepare and phrase drafts. Grading answers and deciding on flags and assessing students remain in human hands and follow published rules.

map.title: Where artificial intelligence is used
map.desc: Browse the tasks of the platform to see which of them use artificial intelligence and which do not.

tasks.title: Lesson from a title
tasks.desc: A proposed lesson is generated from a title chosen by the instructor who then reviews it before publishing.

tasks.title: Lesson from a file
tasks.desc: Lecture material including scanned pages is read and a structured lesson is built from it.

tasks.title: Examinations and homework
tasks.desc: Questions of varied types are proposed with model answers and the instructor selects and edits them.

tasks.title: Course from a presentation
tasks.desc: A presentation is turned into a course of editable units and lessons.

tasks.title: Individual assignment draft
tasks.desc: On request a draft remedial assignment is proposed for one student based on their weaknesses.

tasks.title: Announcement wording
tasks.desc: On request a title and body are suggested for an announcement.

tasks.title: Elaborating recommendations
tasks.desc: Recommendations are derived from fixed rules and their wording is elaborated with AI only on request.

tasks.title: Examination proctoring
tasks.desc: Face and object detection models run inside the student's browser and no image is sent to an external provider.

tasks.title: Grading answers
tasks.desc: Objective questions are graded on the server against model answers and instructors grade essay answers.

tasks.title: Deciding on flags
tasks.desc: The instructor decides every appeal after reviewing the event.

tasks.title: Course analysis
tasks.desc: Strengths and weaknesses are derived by fixed published rules from progress and participation and attendance data.

flow.title: No generated content reaches students without review

steps.title: Source material
steps.desc: The instructor uploads a file or chooses a lesson title.

steps.title: Text extraction
steps.desc: Files are read including scanned pages.

steps.title: Draft preparation
steps.desc: A proposed lesson or examination is generated to a defined structure.

steps.title: Human review
steps.desc: The instructor reviews the draft and edits or rejects it.

steps.title: Release to students
steps.desc: Content is published only by the instructor's decision.

principles.title: Rules that govern the use of artificial intelligence

items.title: Review before release
items.desc: Everything AI generates is a draft until the instructor approves it.

items.title: On request never automatic
items.desc: AI services are not called when pages open but only when a user explicitly asks.

items.title: Fair usage limits
items.desc: Each user has an hourly ceiling on requests to keep the service stable.

items.title: Protecting student images
items.desc: Student images and camera streams are never sent to any AI provider.

items.title: Published rules first
items.desc: Analyses rest on fixed explainable rules and AI is used for wording only.

never.title: What artificial intelligence does not do on the platform
items: It does not grade student answers.
It does not decide on flags or appeals.
It does not see camera streams during examinations.
It does not publish content without the instructor's decision.
